title: Sweeping, Serving, and Caring: How Robots Are Becoming Part of Daily Life
title_zh: 扫地、送餐、陪护：机器人如何融入日常生活
intro_zh: 本文约930词，介绍扫地机器人、餐厅送餐机器人和老年陪护机器人等实例，说明机器人正在逐渐成为日常生活的一部分，语言难度适合CET-4水平。

paragraphs.en: Every morning before going to work, Li Na taps a button on her phone. In her living room, a small round machine sets off and begins sweeping the floor. For Li Na, this robot vacuum is not a high-tech showpiece but a practical home appliance, as normal as her coffee maker. Ten years ago, a robot in the home sounded like science fiction, and most real robots stayed in factories, doing heavy or dangerous jobs. Today, however, service robots are moving into ordinary life. They clean apartments, deliver meals in restaurants and remind older adults to take medicine. Many of them do not look like humans; they are just boxes with wheels and sensors. But these machines are gradually turning imagination into an everyday experience. Industry reports show that home robot sales are increasing by double digits every year in China.
paragraphs.zh: 每天早上去上班之前，李娜都会在手机上轻点一下按钮。客厅里，一台圆形小机器便出发开始清扫地板。对李娜来说，这台扫地机器人并不是用来炫耀的高科技，而是一件实用家电，和咖啡机一样普通。十年前，家里有机器人听起来还像科幻小说，大多数真正的机器人都待在工厂里，从事繁重或危险的工作。而如今，服务机器人正走进日常生活：它们能打扫房间、在餐馆送餐、提醒老人吃药。许多机器人长得并不像人，只是带轮子和传感器的盒子。但这些机器正逐渐把想象变成普通日常。行业报告显示，中国家庭机器人的销量每年都以两位数的速度增长。

paragraphs.en: A good example is Zhang Yun, who works in an office in Hangzhou. When she first unpacked her robot vacuum, she had doubts. The small machine bumped into chairs and spent ten minutes under the sofa. But the robot quickly learned the layout of her apartment. It uses a camera and motion sensors to measure distances and avoid shoes, cables and other obstacles. Now, four months later, Zhang starts the cleaner from her desk at the office. When she returns home, the floor has been dusted and mopped in the corners she used to hate cleaning. She estimates that the machine saves her about one hour every day. 'It does not replace thought, but it does replace worry about dust,' she says. However, she adds that the robot still needs supervision because it cannot climb stairs.
paragraphs.zh: 一个很好的例子是在杭州上班的张芸。刚拆开扫地机器人时，她心里有些怀疑。这个小机器撞到椅子，还在沙发下面待了十分钟。但它很快记住了家里的布局。它利用摄像头和运动传感器测量距离，避开鞋子、电线和其他障碍物。如今，四个月过去，张芸在办公室就能启动清洁器。等她回到家，地板已被打扫干净，连她过去讨厌的角落也被擦拭过。她估计这个机器每天能帮她省下大约一小时。“它不会替人思考，但能让人不再为灰尘发愁，”她说。不过她也补充道，机器人仍需人照看，因为它不会爬楼梯。

paragraphs.en: While some robots stay at home, others have found jobs in public places. In a busy restaurant in Shenzhen, a shelf-shaped robot carries bowls and plates from the kitchen to customers' tables. The machine moves along a planned route but is designed to interact with an ever-changing space. If a waiter suddenly steps into its path, it stops or finds a new way around. Diners can take their dishes directly from the robot, and the robot politely says 'Enjoy your meal.' Restaurant staff are happy to give up repetitive carrying work, because they now have more energy to serve guests personally. The restaurant owner also benefits from the robot, saying that it is cheaper in the long run than hiring extra part-time workers.
paragraphs.zh: 有些机器人留在家里，另一些则在公共场所找到了工作。在深圳一家繁忙的餐馆里，一台货架形状的机器人把碗碟和餐盘从厨房送到顾客桌前。机器按预设路线移动，但被设计成能与不断变化的环境互动。如果服务员突然挡在路上，它会停下或另找路线。顾客可以直接从机器人身上取走饭菜，机器人还会客气地说“请慢用”。员工们很高兴不必再反复跑腿传菜，因为他们能把更多精力用在亲自服务顾客上。店主也因此受益，表示从长远看，比多雇兼职人员更省钱。

paragraphs.en: Such robots seem simple, but behind them lies a useful trick: they sense and act. A robot's camera or laser measures the distance to nearby objects; its software changes that information into commands such as move, turn, or stop. Each time the robot works, it gathers new data and makes its model of the world more accurate. If a chair has been moved from one corner to another, the robot will change its cleaning path rather than hit the chair. This learning process is not always perfect, but small mistakes teach the robot better behavior. Over time, the action becomes quicker and smoother, which is why a robot that was clumsy on its first day may look almost skillful after a week. This continuous improvement is the real source of efficiency in the home.
paragraphs.zh: 这类机器人看起来简单，背后却有一个有用的诀窍：感知，然后行动。机器人的摄像头或激光测量与附近物体的距离；软件把这些信息转成“前进、转弯、停止”等指令。机器人每工作一次，就会收集新数据，让自身对世界的模型更准确。如果一把椅子从一个角落被移到另一个角落，它会调整清扫路线，而不是去撞椅子。这个学习过程并非总是完美，但小失误会让机器人行为更到位。一段时间后，它的动作会更快更流畅，这也是为什么头一天还笨手笨脚的机器人一周后会显得很熟练。这种不断改进正是家庭生活中效率的真正来源。

paragraphs.en: Another carefully designed robot is becoming familiar to elderly people who live alone. Seventy-year-old Chen Jun in Shanghai shares his apartment with what he calls his little nurse. This device is a tabletop companion. Throughout the day, it announces when it is time to drink water or take medicine. It can also detect unusual events: if Chen falls and does not rise, the robot contacts his daughter through a video call. At night, it can play old songs and tell stories. Chen says the robot is not a substitute for human company, but it makes his home feel less empty. His daughter agrees. She wants to work in another city, but now she can at least know that her father has a watchful helper while she is away.
paragraphs.zh: 另一类精心设计的机器人正逐渐被独居老人熟悉。上海70岁的陈军与被他称为“小护士”的机器一起生活。这台设备是桌上型伙伴。一天中，它会播报该喝水或吃药的时间。它还能觉察异常：如果陈军跌倒后没有站起来，机器人会通过视频通话联系他的女儿。到了晚上，它会播放老歌、讲故事。陈军说，机器人并不能代替人的陪伴，但让家不那么空。他女儿也同意：她想在外地工作，但至少现在知道，自己不在身边时，父亲有一个警觉的帮手。

paragraphs.en: Robots can also play with children, although adults should think carefully about why. Some educational robots now on the market listen to a child's questions, tell stories, and even encourage children to practice English. They are usually designed as friendly cartoon animals, with big eyes that light up when they hear a correct answer. Such toys can make learning playful and may help children spend less time staring at screens. But education specialists point out that robots are still machines. They can offer information, but they cannot understand a child's feelings deeply. Real conversation, eye contact, and hugs remain vital for healthy development. Therefore, parents should use robots as tools, not as replacements for themselves.
paragraphs.zh: 机器人也能陪孩子玩，不过成年人应该认真思考为什么用它们。市场上部分教育机器人能听懂孩子的问题、讲故事，甚至鼓励孩子练习英语。它们常被设计成友善的卡通动物，听到正确答案时大眼睛会亮起来。这类玩具能寓教于乐，还可能帮助孩子少盯屏幕。但教育专家指出，机器人终究是机器：它们能提供资料，却不能真正理解孩子的情感。真实的对话、眼神交流与拥抱对健康成长依然至关重要。因此，父母应把机器人当作工具，而不是自己的替代品。

paragraphs.en: Of course, welcoming robots into daily life does not mean ignoring the risks. Some families worry that cameras and sensors on these machines constantly monitor their movements, turning home privacy into a new challenge. A hacked robot could expose personal images or data. Other people fear that robots may injure children or pets if their software makes a wrong judgment. Designers therefore are trying to set strict safety standards. For example, a robot must brake immediately when it detects a hand or an animal in its way. Privacy protection is another key point: data collected by the machine should be stored safely or deleted after use. There is also concern about job losses, but history shows that technology tends to remove old tasks while creating new opportunities.
paragraphs.zh: 当然，欢迎机器人进入生活并不等于对风险视而不见。有些家庭担心机器上的摄像头和传感器会不断监控自己的行动，让家里的私密性变成新问题；被黑客入侵的机器人还可能泄露个人影像或数据。还有人担心机器人可能因为算法误判而伤到孩子或宠物。因此，设计人员正努力制定严格的安全标准：例如，机器人一旦检测到手或动物在面前，必须立刻刹车。隐私保护也很关键——机器收集的数据应当安全存储或在使用后删除。此外还有对失业的担忧，但历史表明，技术往往在淘汰旧任务的同时创造新机会。

paragraphs.en: Looking around our homes and neighborhoods, the first generation of everyday robots is far from perfect. They cannot hold deep conversations or handle complicated household tasks such as folding laundry. But their growing popularity shows that people are ready to share a little space with machines. In return, these machines offer what we value most in modern life: time. By taking over dull or exhausting tasks, they give us more chances to enjoy a meal with family, focus on work, or read a book. The day may not be far when the sound of a robot sweeping floors is as familiar as the sound of a kettle boiling. There will be challenges ahead, but if robots are designed with care, the next chapter of daily life could be both convenient and human-centered.
paragraphs.zh: 环顾我们的家和社区，第一代日常机器人还远远谈不上完美：它们无法进行深入对话，也难以完成叠衣服这类复杂的家务。但它们渐渐流行，说明人们愿意让机器在生活空间里占一席之地。而作为回报，这些机器提供的是现代生活中我们最重视的东西：时间。机器承担了枯燥或累人的工作，让我们有更多机会与家人共享一顿饭、专心工作，或读一本书。机器人清扫地面的声音有朝一日也许会像水壶烧开的声响一样普通。前路仍有挑战，但只要用心设计机器人，日常生活的下一章完全可能既便捷又以人为本。

questions.q: What is the passage mainly about?
options: A. It introduces how service robots are becoming common helpers in daily life.
B. It argues that robots should replace human workers in restaurants.
C. It compares robot vacuums with educational robots in detail.
D. It explains how to repair home robots safely.
questions.explain: 主旨题。全文以吸尘机器人、餐厅送餐机器人、老人陪伴机器人和教育机器人为例，说明服务机器人正逐渐融入日常生活，因此选A。

questions.q: According to the passage, which of the following is true about the delivery robot in the Shenzhen restaurant?
options: A. It cooks meals and serves them one by one.
B. It follows the waiters and opens doors for them.
C. It works only in the kitchen, not in the dining area.
D. It moves among people and carries dishes safely.
questions.explain: 细节题。第三段提到机器从厨房送餐到餐桌，遇到服务员会停下或绕行；D项“在人群中移动并安全送餐”与此相符。

questions.q: What can be inferred about educational robots from Paragraph 6?
options: A. They are too expensive for most families.
B. They can take over parents' role completely.
C. They are useful, but adults still need to guide children.
D. They should be used only in schools.
questions.explain: 推断题。第六段说教育机器人能激发兴趣，但专家提醒它们不能代替真实的人际交流，父母仍要参与和引导，因此选C。

questions.q: The word 'monitor' in Paragraph 7 is closest in meaning to:
questions.explain: 词义题。第七段说摄像头和传感器会不断“监控”用户活动；monitor在文中作动词，意为“监测、监控”，与watch over同义，因此选B。
